papers.title: Neural mechanisms underlying the effects of cognitive fatigue on physical effort-based choice.
papers.reason: Uses computational modelling of human effort-based choice with fMRI during cognitive fatigue induced by a working-memory task, directly relevant to modelling executive control and decision making.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Alpha-Band Oscillations as Potential Indicators of Executive Subcomponents Dysfunction correlating to the Severity of Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.reason: Examines resting-state EEG alpha-band markers of inhibitory control and working-memory deficits in CSVD with screening-performance analyses for executive dysfunction.

papers.title: Negatively valenced stimuli selectively enhance frontal midline theta during inhibitory control.
papers.reason: Directly reports EEG frontal-midline-theta findings during inhibitory control and emotional modulation, providing clear neural constraints for cognitive-control models.

papers.title: Wavelets and switching in bistable visual perception: Comment on "Wavelet analysis in biomedical research: A versatile tool for multiscale signal characterization and functional connectivity analysis" by Kralj et al․.
papers.reason: Discusses EEG wavelet and connectivity approaches for bistable perception and selective attention, but it is a methodological comment rather than a primary executive-function study.

papers.title: Multidimensional EEG Feature Fusion and Interpretable Machine Learning for Identifying Cognitive Impairment in Depression.
papers.reason: Develops an interpretable resting-state EEG machine-learning classifier for cognitive impairment in depression, but the cognitive outcome is broad MoCA status rather than executive function specifically.

papers.title: Case Report: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke: a diagnostic challenge and biomarker-based clarification.
papers.reason: Reports a clinical diagnostic case of rapidly progressive dementia using MRI, CSF, and EEG biomarkers without meaningful focus on executive-function modelling or assessment.
